problem: The company had little money for marketing.
title: Hotmail adds a free-email tagline to every message sent by its users
context: Hotmail launched free web email in 1996 with a small venture round of about $300,000.
decision_made: Append a tagline inviting recipients to get free email at Hotmail to every outgoing message.
action_taken: Investor Tim Draper pushed for the tagline; the founders initially resisted altering users' email.
observed_outcome: Hotmail reportedly passed 100,000 subscribers in its first 30 days and a million within six months; Microsoft later bought it in a deal reported at about $400 million. User counts at sale differ by source.
lessons: Building the marketing into the product itself can produce growth with almost no budget.
limitations: User-count figures conflict (1 million, 10 million or 12 million at sale depending on source). The exact "P.S. I love you" wording was not confirmed. The sale price is reported, not confirmed.

claims.claim_text: A tagline was added to every Hotmail message after an investor pushed for it.
Hotmail grew quickly and was sold to Microsoft in a deal reported at about $400 million.
